judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Exclamatory comic offer with a tidy setup-complaint-hook arc and a joke simile ('worse than a hailstorm'); the ambient lines all point back at the same Ogre gag, too neatly themed for a Westwood town.

items.label: B
items.critique: Flat, slightly stiff innkeeper prose ('somewhat slow of late'), the bare '100 in gold' reward and a one-line journal; the guard and rumour lines are plain information drops, very Nox.

items.label: C
items.critique: The warden with a 'signed and sealed' notice and the 'never had to set one foot inside' punchline is constructed comedy; the offer is long and closes on an over-explained location-plus-goal formula.

items.label: D
items.critique: Overwrought pleading ('a horrific fate has befallen my wife'), 'kind sir', the slightly broken possessive in the journal and the deadpan cider joke all read as the original campaign.

items.label: E
items.critique: Magic shears and winter coats is a whimsical premise built for a joke; 'My tongue's stuck to the railing!' and the cold-weather guard quip feel like a modern writer's flavour pass.

items.label: F
items.critique: Mayor's spider quest with the 'charm' instruction, the title and freedom-of-passage reward, the gate guard and the 'right off you back' typo are characteristic of Westwood's early town.

items.label: G
items.critique: Bombastic 'in defense of Nox's vital interests', a key and a beast scroll handed over mid-speech, a numbered journal objective and the pushy 'Buy something!' shopkeeper are pure Nox.

items.label: H
items.critique: The singed-beard teacher is a crafted comic bit ('Don't look at my chin!') with another 'worse than a plague of rats' simile; the reward line is fussy and the whole town riffs on one wizard theme.

items.label: I
items.critique: Repetitive 'mate', 'a damn fine spell', the long literal journal sentence and the cross-referencing mayor-spider gossip are the original's plain, slightly clumsy voice.

items.label: J
items.critique: The Urchin-in-a-big-hat con, the arch journal ('before it's sold again') and the courtroom-pun guard ('her floor testifies to it') are too witty and too polished for Nox's townsfolk.

tells: New texts build each quest around a single comic premise (a swindle, a singed beard, a squatter eviction) and then make the guard, shop and townsfolk lines all riff on that same joke; Westwood's ambient lines are about the wider world (bandits, checkpoints, rumours, the war) and rarely echo the quest.

New offers follow a uniform three-beat shape: exclamatory complaint, comic detail with a 'worse than X' simile, then a precise location plus 'and I'll reward you'; Westwood's offers are flatter, more literal, and hand over items or keys mid-speech.
New thanks lines carry a punchline or callback; Westwood's thanks are generic gratitude plus the reward ('take this gold as payment', '100 in gold').
Westwood's journals are bare or clumsily literal (sometimes a typo or numbered objective); new journals are neat imperatives or add a wry tag.

Westwood lets small errors and stiff phrasing through ('right off you back', 'somewhat slow of late', 'in defense of Nox's vital interests'); new texts are uniformly clean and clever, with wordplay and quips for every bystander.
